# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (stated as budget holder)
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, a twelve-week structured implementation program within the AI Governance Academy
**Fee:** US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff.

The Client's AI use cases are recorded in three stages:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The Client's AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The regulatory drivers recorded are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The certification target is ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year, although that start date is not fixed.

An internal audit finding of June 2026 records that there is no inventory of AI systems.

Dana Whitfield's stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The stated constraints are:

* budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year
* customer data must stay in the EU
* the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

This proposal sets out how the Guided AI GRC Build would deliver a minimum viable Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) within twelve weeks. The Client's own team would build it, own it and operate it.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement typically hands over a finished set of documents. A guided build works differently: the Client's standing build team produces every artifact itself, with weekly coaching and review from the program.

Three outcomes follow from this approach.

* **The team understands the system.** The people who will run the AIMS have built each register, policy and workflow themselves. They therefore understand why each element exists.
* **The system can be operated without dependency.** Evidence collection begins during the program, not after it. This means the operating routines are tested by the people who will maintain them.
* **The team can extend the system.** The planned sales forecasting use case, and the ISO/IEC 42001 work the Client intends to start next year, can be taken forward by the Client's team using the same methods and assets.

The program runs on three principles: **Slow AI**, **Informed Intent** and **Final Liability rests with the Human**. In practice, every AI system in scope has a named human accountable for its outcomes. Each deployment decision is made deliberately and is recorded.

The working frameworks are:

* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Steering material draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Order of inventory entry (Week 2).** Systems enter the inventory in the following order, for the reasons given.

1. **The customer service chatbot enters first.** It is the only use case recorded as deployed, so it is the system already in use.
2. **AI visual inspection on the German production line enters second.** It is the use case tied to the stated Q2 2027 objective, and it is subject to the works council constraint.
3. **AI sales forecasting is registered as a planned entry.** Recording it now allows it to pass through intake and classification before it is built.

**Mapping to ISO/IEC 42001 and incumbent frameworks.** Each week's artifacts are mapped to ISO/IEC 42001 readiness themes. This mapping supports readiness work only and does not promise certification.

The incumbent frameworks recorded are an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. The Profile Block does not name the specific registers, procedures or records within these frameworks. For that reason, integration points are shown as `Unknown` until intake confirms them. The one exception is Week 2, which attaches to the June 2026 internal audit finding.

| Week | Spine focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Incumbent integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Draft the AIMS charter and assign accountable humans per use case; first steering checkpoint | Context, scope and leadership (Clauses 4 and 5) | Unknown |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Inventory the chatbot, then visual inspection, then forecasting as a planned entry | Scope and AI system resources (Clause 4.3; Annex A.4) | Inventory as the artifact responding to the June 2026 internal audit finding |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | Classify each use case against the EU AI Act and define risk criteria; confirm with external counsel | Risk criteria (Clause 6.1) | Unknown |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Assess the chatbot and visual inspection, including GDPR considerations and production staff impacts; confirm with external counsel | AI risk assessment and AI system impact assessment (Clauses 6.1.2 and 6.1.4; Annex A.5) | Unknown |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Stand up the operating AI risk register with treatment owners | AI risk treatment (Clause 6.1.3) | Unknown |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Draft and route the core policy set for adoption; mid-point steering | AI policy (Clause 5.2; Annex A.2) | Unknown |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Define lifecycle gates for moving visual inspection from pilot to production | AI system lifecycle (Annex A.6) | Unknown |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Assess suppliers behind each use case, including where customer data is processed relative to the EU constraint | Third-party relationships and documented information (Annex A.10; Clause 7.5) | Unknown |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Bring at least two AI workflows under governance with defined human oversight | Use of AI systems and operational control (Annex A.9; Clause 8) | Unknown |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Define evaluation and monitoring for each governed workflow | Monitoring and measurement (Clause 9.1) | Unknown |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Define AI incident and change routes, then review four weeks of evidence | Nonconformity and planning of changes (Clauses 10.2 and 6.3) | Unknown |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Hold an evidence walkthrough with the build team, then closing steering | Internal audit and management review readiness (Clauses 9.2 and 9.3) | Unknown |

**Works council timing.** Any step in Weeks 4, 7 or 9 that touches production staff will be sequenced after the German works council has been consulted, as the stated constraint requires. The legal requirements for that consultation should be confirmed with external counsel.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS. It consists of six elements:

1. adopted charter
2. populated inventory
3. operating risk register
4. adopted core policy set
5. at least two governed AI workflows in production use
6. evidence collection running for at least four weeks

**Scope of the outcome.** This is a readiness outcome. It is not a certification, audit or regulatory compliance outcome.

**The second governed workflow.** The chatbot is the only use case recorded as deployed. Visual inspection is recorded as piloting, with production targeted for Q2 2027. The second governed workflow in production use therefore needs to be confirmed at intake (see Section 8).

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The build team is drawn from the following roles:

* General Counsel
* CISO
* Head of Quality
* Head of Data
* German plant manager
* two internal auditors

The hours below are **estimates** of weekly commitment per person. They cover the live workshop, coaching and asynchronous work. Actual effort will depend on scope decisions made at intake.

| Role | Typical week (estimate) | Peak weeks and peak hours (estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 hours | Weeks 1, 3, 6 and 12: 5 to 6 hours |
| CISO | 3 to 4 hours | Weeks 4, 8 and 11: 5 to 6 hours |
| Head of Quality | 3 to 4 hours | Weeks 7, 10 and 11: 5 to 6 hours |
| Head of Data | 4 to 5 hours | Weeks 2, 4 and 10: 6 to 7 hours |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 hours | Weeks 4, 7 and 9: 4 to 5 hours |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 hours | Weeks 2, 11 and 12: 3 to 4 hours |

**Role of the internal auditors.** The program will agree the internal auditors' role at intake. The aim is to preserve their independence for any later internal audit of the AIMS.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints are held at Weeks 1, 6 and 12.

| Week | Checkpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization brief | Confirms scope, team, risks to delivery and the decisions needed |
| 6 | Mid-point report | Reviews spine status, blockers and scope decisions |
| 12 | Closing report | Attests the minimum viable AIMS against the six-element definition and sets out a 12-month operating plan |

**Attendees.** Steering attendees are `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Weekly format.**

* one live virtual workshop
* one coaching session
* structured asynchronous implementation between sessions

**Duration.** Twelve weeks.

**Data handling.** Customer data must stay in the EU. To respect this constraint:

* no customer data will be shared in program sessions
* Client artifacts and evidence will be stored in a location the Client designates

The storage location is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

**Fee.** US$60,000. This sits within the budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

**Payment and contract.** The payment schedule is `Unknown`. Contract terms carry legal effect and should be confirmed with external counsel.

## 8. Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. Which start date places Week 12 before the planned Q2 2027 production date for visual inspection? Does that date fall within the current fiscal year for budget purposes?
2. Which second AI workflow can be in governed production use by Week 12?
3. Does the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS hold a risk register, supplier assessment or incident process that AIMS artifacts should attach to?
4. Does the ISO 9001 quality management system hold change control or nonconformity procedures relevant to visual inspection?
5. Does the chatbot process customer data? If so, where is that data processed?
6. When will the German works council be consulted, and what is the consultation route?
7. Who attends each steering checkpoint, and what role will the internal auditors hold?

## 9. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a 60-minute scoping call with Dana Whitfield before that date to work through the intake questions and fix a start date. The program would then issue the Week 1 mobilization brief.
